summary: Builds a length-limited Huffman decoding table (per the LEGACY ABI name Huffman_Compression_Tree_Builder, consistent with the observed structure). Lazily allocates a 1492-byte working buffer through the object's allocation routine dispatched via the function pointer at a1+4, caching it in *a3; retains the 16-byte input count array a2 at buffer offset +208. RLE-expands the 16 counts into a local symbol-length sequence, computes the canonical Huffman code start-index table, writes the tree rows at buffer offsets +4/+72/+144, and populates a fast-decode table pair at offsets +212 (symbols) and +1236 (length bytes) for bit lengths 7..0.

local_names.a1: object whose allocation routine is dispatched through the function pointer stored at a1+4
local_names.a2: pointer to the 16-byte input count array (per-length Huffman symbol counts)
local_names.a3: pointer to the output buffer slot; lazily allocated with a 1492-byte block when null
local_names.v3: working Huffman table buffer (the allocated 1492-byte block)

operations.description: If the output slot *a3 is null, allocate the working buffer lazily before any use.
Invoke the allocation routine through the function pointer stored at a1+4 (object vtable slot) with arguments (a1, 1, 1492), and store the returned buffer address into *a3.
Store the input 16-byte count array pointer a2 at byte offset +208 of the working buffer so the counts are retained for later passes.

Pass 1 (i = 1..16): read each input count byte a2[i] and RLE-expand by appending symbol i repeated a2[i] times into the local length-sequence buffer v29, using a memset32 fill of the repeated-byte pattern.
Pass 2: walk the expanded length sequence and compute the canonical Huffman code start-index table v28, doubling the running code value at each length boundary (standard canonical code construction).
Pass 3 (lengths 1..16): write the tree rows for each present length, storing the start index at +4 and +144 and the end index at +72 (b[1], b[36], b[18]); absent lengths store -1 at +72.
Write 0xFFFFF to +136 (b[34]) and zero-fill the 0x400-byte symbol table starting at +212 (b+53).

Pass 4 (bit lengths j = 7..0): for each length level, fill the fast-decode lookup spans of size 1<<j: store the symbol at the table slot b[start+53] (+212 region) and the length byte at (char*)b + start + 1236, for every symbol at that length.
Return the last processed code value (result).
